sections.changelog:
Changed

  • **A part number the catalogue does not carry now ends the search and says so.** The last attempt used to release the number and answer with whatever the remaining words matched, on the reasoning that products beat a dead end. On a parts catalogue that reasoning inverts: the number names the device the part has to fit, and a listing gives the shopper no way to see that the parts on screen fit a different one. Measured on a 12 460-product shop, an unstocked code answered with ten unrelated parts and no sign that the code was never found. The dropdown now says so instead — "No product with that number. Try another query.", or the shop's own empty-state wording where one is set — and withholds the categories, brands and best-sellers it would otherwise offer, since each is the same substitution under another name. The number still has to be missing outright, and the rescues get their turn first: a query whose number exists but whose other words do not still relaxes down to the products carrying that number, and a mistyped or wrong-layout code is still recovered before anything ends. Measured against a shop's own search log — 499 phrases, 1 280 searches — eighteen phrases named a number nothing in the catalogue could satisfy, fourteen of them were recovered by the layout swap or the typo pass, and four reached the new dead end: 0.3% of the searches, each of which used to answer with parts for another device. Search-as-you-type is unaffected while the number is on its way somewhere — a half-typed code that still prefixes something in the catalogue stays a keystroke rather than a requirement, and only one that prefixes nothing ends the search. Turning off model discipline restores the old behaviour wholesale.

Fixed

  • **A search is now one pass over the index, not a descent of identical ones.** Coverage relaxation, the layout-swap retry, the typo retry and the zero-result ladder each stepped a floor down one rung at a time, running the whole ranking statement again on every rung — same terms, same joins, same scoring, same sort, same limit, differing only in the `matched >= N` its HAVING demanded. On a phrase the descent is the whole cost: measured on a 14 800-product catalogue, "шлейф разъема зарядки нижняя плата samsung galaxy a52 оригинал новый качественный" ran that statement eighteen times for 2 906 ms, and "дисплей в сборе с тачскрином для iphone 11 pro max черный оригинал" four times for 1 745 ms. Since the sort leads with coverage, a strict rung is the head of the loose one, so a single pass at the floor carries every rung above it and the descent became a filter on a column the rows already return. Same catalogue, same queries: 2 906 → 160 ms and 1 745 → 105 ms, and the worst case fell from `W + 2⌊W/3⌋ + 3` statements to at most one per retry branch. Verified against the previous build across 28 runs in all three stock modes and with click boost and title-only coverage on: identical results, identical order, identical coverage figures.
  • **The model number now narrows the search instead of being checked at the end.** A word carrying a digit is pinned as required, and the requirement was stated in HAVING — a figure the aggregation has already paid for. So a query naming a model still scored every object sharing any word with it and threw the result away: on a 12 460-product catalogue "…samsung galaxy a52…" aggregated 9 021 objects, 72% of the shop. The same demand is now also stated in WHERE as a semi-join, so the pass starts from the 65 objects that carry the model: 671 → 111 ms on that statement. Queries naming no model are untouched.
  • **The click boost no longer joins a table it has nothing to find in.** The join was added whenever the boost is enabled, and with no click logged for that query the multiplier it computes is exactly 1.0 — a lookup per candidate row to multiply by one. It is now preceded by a primary-key probe for the query's hash: 572 → 455 ms on a shop whose clicks table held seven rows, with the outcome unchanged.
  • **Sold-out demotion no longer decides which results survive the limit.** It sorted ahead of relevance in SQL, so on a catalogue with many stocked partial matches the window could fill with them and drop the exact match the shopper typed, purely because it was sold out. Ranking now happens first and the demotion is applied to the rows that come back. The order delivered is the same — stocked first, then coverage, then score, exactly as the query used to sort it — and what changes is which rows reach that order at all, but only on a query matching more than the scanned head (a hundred rows in the dropdown, the results ceiling on the page): below that every match is in the window either way. This is also what lets one pass stand in for the whole descent, since coverage now leads the sort.
  • **The results page caches its ranked pool.** The dropdown has been cached since the first release; the page behind it never was, so every Enter, every sort and every page of pagination re-ran the ranking — at up to a thousand rows rather than the dropdown's ten. Only the pool is stored, for the same five minutes and under the same cache version, so a product edit clears both surfaces at once; the shopper's sort, price range and facets still apply to it afterwards.
